question: At the fixed published-R17 panel fibres, how often do generic degree-one translated-bisection intersections account for simultaneous cover splitting, and how many quotient directions can those relations leave?
family_wide_rule: For every unordered pair of distinct native atlas covers with traces wi,wj, retain the translates S=(R+wi+wj)/2 where R is a norm-six vector in wi+wj+2M, modulo simultaneous conjugation. The corresponding translated bisections have intersection number one, hence one rational component of length one. This rule uses only generic lattice data.
evaluation: Evaluate the rule only at the 165 existing published-R17 addresses in the frozen census. Because a relation incidence at a smooth, nonbranch fibre implies both native covers split there, it suffices to enumerate the 519 co-split pairs. This is lazy evaluation of the same full-atlas rule, not a rank-selected pair population. Do not compute other intersection parameters.
method: Freeze the 118 relevant generic lift maps and trace vectors by streaming the existing atlas. Enumerate short representatives of each distinct trace-sum parity coset, with checkpoints. At each existing fibre check all four branch choices by exact elliptic group arithmetic against both conjugate translates. Record signed quotient relations, their exact rank, and the resulting upper bound on the native quotient span. Distinguish globally forced degree-one intersections from those occurring at the tested parameter.
failure_semantics: Timeout leaves the affected count UNKNOWN and preserves completed coset/fibre checkpoints. Absence of a norm-six relation does not exclude another relation or global solubility. Pair relations identify quotient lines and are not evidence for independent new directions. Ranks remain inherited subgroup bounds; no prospective selection policy is changed.
